simulated_decision: Weak Accept / Borderline Accept after format conversion
summary: The paper now has an official AAAI-2026 anonymous-submission LaTeX branch that compiles successfully to an 8-page PDF. This removes a major formatting blocker from the previous iteration. The strongest remaining risks are empirical rather than textual: missing complete CAST/StyTr2/AesFA/AesPA-Net matched runs, no human preference study, and timing not yet measured under a fully controlled benchmark.
improvements_since_iter4: Downloaded the official AAAI-2026 author kit through the working authorkit26-1 endpoint.
Created an independent aaai_submission branch without overwriting the full article-style working draft.
Converted the preamble to use aaai2026.sty and aaai2026.bst, removing disallowed article packages such as geometry, hyperref, and fontenc.
Compiled the official-template draft successfully to an 8-page PDF.
Reduced major table/long-name overfull issues; only one small equation overfull remains.
current_strengths: Core claim is bounded and evidence-backed.
SaMST artifact story is supported by both visual grids and artifact-sensitive metrics.
Ablations and sweep results give a credible mechanism-level explanation.
remaining_rejection_risks: Reviewers may object that CAST and StyTr2 are only smoke-tested, not complete matched baselines.
The SaMST cleanliness claim still needs human preference validation if used as a main narrative point.
Raw CLIP-style is not higher than SaMST; the paper must keep framing around style-content-cleanliness trade-off rather than raw style dominance.
References need a final metadata audit before submission.
The draft was prepared with AI assistance and must be treated as an internal draft subject to author rewriting and policy compliance.

acceptance_readiness.overall: credible weak-accept draft, but not safe without missing baseline/user-study upgrades
